I have a very impulsive personality that has lead me to many addictions through out my life. Smoking, drinking, sugar, coffee, energy drinks, gaming, to name but a few. It is only recently that I have found a way to take control of my impulsiveness and managed to subside all my addictions/habits (except smoking). The method that's worked for me is meditation.

Your thoughts are like a conveyor belt, one rolls along, lifts off the conveyor for a moment and takes centre stage, then goes back on. The challenge is, when an addictive thought has taken centre stage, can you resist acting on it. I have come to believe meditation is the process of keeping your thoughts on the conveyor belt, acknowledging its there, but letting it pass by. It's about keeping a clear mind and being in control of your thought, not the other way around.

The technique I started with was focusing on my breathing, some like to concentrate on the feeling of breath in your throat, others like the feeling at the tip of the nose. What ever works best. The aim is to clear your mind onto nothing but the sensation of your breathing, your mind will wander onto other thoughts, its natural. Now the measure of how well you are doing is how long it takes you to acknowledge you are deep in another thought, gently try and bring your mind back to the sensation of your breath. It takes a lot of practice, but it's worth it to be in full control.

When you have a think of a memory, you are activating the neural pathways associated with the memory, you modify them and make them more prominent (why memories become corrupted over time). When you think of a memory you can think of an input coming from your minds eye (the internal monologue). When you hear, smell, see something, they are all inputs to, triggering memory pathways which you then use together to construct an understanding of what you are sensing.
